protocol.name: tileception_dashboard_v1
protocol.copyright: Part of Tileception. Any client may implement it.
protocol.description:
A plugin with a [dashboard] block that sets surface = true is started with WAYLAND_SOCKET, a connection Tileception made for it alone. That connection offers wl_compositor, wl_subcompositor, wl_shm, wp_viewporter and this global, and nothing else: no windows, no input devices, no clipboard, no outputs, no screen capture.
The plugin lists its items in its tileception://dashboard resource. For each item of type "surface" it creates a wl_surface and passes it to get_item with the item's id. Tileception chooses where the item goes and how large it is, tells the plugin in a configure event, clips what the plugin draws to that size and frames it with the item's title and the plugin's name.
Frame callbacks arrive only while the item is on screen, so a plugin that draws on each frame callback costs nothing while the dashboard is hidden. The surface gets pointer motion, buttons and scroll while the pointer is over it, and never the keyboard.

interface.name: tileception_dashboard_v1
interface.description: The global for drawing dashboard items.

entry.name: role
entry.summary: the surface already has a role

entry.name: taken
entry.summary: the item already has a surface

entry.name: too_many
entry.summary: the plugin already has six items

request.name: get_item

description.summary: draw an item with this surface

request.description: Gives the surface the dashboard item role. The item is the one with this id among the plugin's surface items; until the plugin lists it, the item is not shown. An item has one surface at a time.

arg.name: item
arg.summary: the item's id in the plugin's resource

interface.name: tileception_dashboard_item_v1
interface.description: Draw at the size of the last configure event, with the buffer scale it gives. Content beyond that size is not shown.

request.name: destroy
request.description: The surface loses its role; the item shows a placeholder.

event.name: configure
event.description: The size in logical pixels and the buffer scale to draw at, sent when the item is placed and whenever either changes. A size of 0 by 0 means the item is not placed now, for instance when it does not fit; keep the last buffer.
